title: finding(gate): all three copies of objectui#7448's document-count pin read workflow headers — none reads a gate `.mjs` docblock, which is where the last two rotted counts were
body:
Found while implementing objectui#8484 (the package-README census in `check-doc-component-types.mjs`' header read "26 across 12 files"; the true reading is 26 across 8). Not fixed there: that card's surface is one paragraph of one gate, and this is the class question. Filed rather than folded in.

## The gap

objectui#7448 ruled that a count copied into a header rots, and gave the class a mechanical half: the `documentCounts` / `POPULATION_COUNT` pin. Three copies exist today — `check-doc-component-types.test.ts:64`, `check-doc-fence-languages.test.ts:54`, `check-links-workflow.test.ts:132`.

**Every one of them reads a workflow YAML header** (the third also reads its own test file's header). Grepped on `c30026715`: the string `documentCounts(` appears only against `headerComments(workflowYaml())`, `commentProse(workflowYaml())` and `ownHeaderComment()`. Positive control in the same run: `POPULATION_COUNT` itself is found 3 times, one per copy, so the zero is a property of the surface and not of a grep that missed.

⇒ **No copy reads a gate `.mjs` docblock**, and that is where the counts that actually rot are living. Two instances landed there in the last week alone:

- `check-shell-escape-residue.mjs:232` — "203 of today's 207 files", true 202/206 (objectui#8122, closed).
- `check-doc-component-types.mjs:287` — "26 unregistered `type` literals across 12 files", true 8 (objectui#8484). This one had already been quoted onward into objectui#8115's brief, which instructs its implementer not to re-derive the census.

objectui#8122 named the gap in passing and fixed its own two sites; objectui#7966 (open) and objectui#7901 (closed) are the same family pointed at `content/docs/**` prose. **`scripts/*.mjs` gate docblocks are the sibling surface none of them covers.**

## The part that makes this a design question, measured

A verbatim extension does not work, and here is the reading rather than the guess. The pin's own pattern, applied unchanged to the comment prose of the three doc gates on `c30026715`:

```
scripts/check-doc-component-types.mjs   34036 prose chars   6 hits
scripts/check-doc-fence-languages.mjs   15424 prose chars   2 hits
scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs     92068 prose chars   8 hits
```

Most of those 16 are **legitimate and cannot rot**, because they are dated readings rather than live claims:

- `check-doc-fence-languages.mjs:345` — "`273537957`: 83 files, 105 blocks" — a count anchored to a commit.
- `check-doc-snippet-types.mjs:704` and `:771` — a count quoted *as the example of a count that went stale*, which is a quotation, not a claim.
- `check-doc-component-types.mjs:89` — "Measured over all 143 files on ..." — a stated measurement point.

So the question the card has to answer is the one the pattern cannot: **how does a check tell a dated reading from a live claim?** The two candidate answers already present in this tree, both worth costing before either is built:

1. **Require the anchor.** A numeral qualifying a document-population noun is a finding *unless* the same sentence names a commit or a re-derivation command. That is the shape objectui#8484 used for its fix and the shape `check-doc-fence-languages.mjs:345` already uses. It has a real false-positive tail (the quotation case above would still fire).
2. **Re-derive and compare.** The test re-runs the instrument and asserts the header's numbers equal today's reading. No hard-coded expected value, fails exactly when the measurement moves — but it turns every README/doc edit into a comment edit, and it only works where an instrument is cheap to re-run.

⛔ Neither is obviously right, which is why this is filed rather than implemented.

## Why it is worth a card

Nothing goes red on any of it. The class has now produced instances in `content/docs` prose (objectui#7965, objectui#7886), in workflow headers (objectui#7825, objectui#7448), and twice in gate docblocks (objectui#8122, objectui#8484) — and the docblock instances are the worst of the three, because a gate's docblock is what the next author of that gate reads before moving its scan population, and in objectui#8484's case the wrong number had already been copied into a dispatch brief that told its reader not to check it.
